newsitem.title: USA: Galileo reservation system sets $700 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Galileo reservation system sets $700 million deal.

text.p: Galileo International Partnership, an electronic reservations company owned by several airlines, said Tuesday it agreed with United Airlines and other carriers to buy marketing group Apollo Travel Services for $700 million.

Galileo, which lets travel agencies access schedule and fare information, book reservations and issue tickets for 525 airlines, also said it filed an initial public offering plan with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Rosemont, Ill.-based Galileo, which also provides car rental and hotel reservation services, said its current 11 airline owners -- including United -- will each retain an ownership interest in the company after the offering.
Under the Apollo deal, Galileo will pay $539 million for United's 77 percent stake in Apollo, which markets Galileo's computer reservation services in the United States, Mexico, and the Caribbean.
Galileo also agreed to buy US Airways' 21 percent stake and Air Canada's 2 percent stakes in Apollo, bringing the total value of the deal to $700 million.
In addition, Galileo may pay United up to $154 million more in the sixth year following the sale under a services agreement to help Galileo expand the Apollo business.
Apollo also manages the communications network that connects travel agency computers with Galileo's system.
United, US Airways and Air Canada currently own about 38 percent, 11 percent and 1 percent of Galileo, respectively. Eight other international airlines own the balance.

United, a unit of Chicago-based UAL Corp., said it does not plan to sell any of its shares in Galileo as part of the initial public offering and expects to retain a significant ownership percentage after the IPO's completion.

United Chairman Gerald Greenwald said in a statement the Apollo sale would allow United to concentrate on its core businesses, retain its substantial ownership stake in Galileo and realize a major, one-time cash infusion.
"In the long term, United intends to invest the proceeds from the sale of ATS (Apollo) in such a manner as to increase shareholder value by increasing earnings per share," the company said.

Galileo said it would use the proceeds from the initial public offering to provide part of the financing for the acquisition of Apollo. It also will use part of the proceeds to buy the Dutch and Swiss marketing companies for its services, Galileo Nederland B.V. and Traviswiss, which are owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and Swissair AG, respectively.

"We believe that Galileo International's decision to acquire ATS (Apollo Travel) is a sound one, made in the best interests of all parties," James Barlett, president of Galileo International, said in a statement.
"Our combined resources will create an even more customer-focused organization that will enable us to better serve our customer base."
